reviewed_version: Supplied publisher version of record, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01379-0; 47 PDF pages, printed245–291; online2025-10-10
summary: A complete analytic n=2 counterexample falsifies the strict positivity in the broader Section2 range; the main n≥3 theorem is not refuted. The inspected shooting, singular-node, phase and tail steps yield no additional substantive defect.

findings.title: Proposition2.5(iii) is not strictly positive throughout the enlarged n>1 range

source_locations.claim: Section2 permits real n in(1,infinity); C1-C4
P2 definition(2.20), C7, strict positivity and critical-point proof
Finite-zero argument valid for the cubic n=2 example

findings.method: Analytic counterexample with a precisely defined real initial datum; no numerical computation.
findings.parameters: n=2, f(s)=s^3-s. Let w0 solve w0''+w0'/t+w0^3=0, w0(0)=1,w0'(0)=0. Let c- be its first negative minimum and c+ its following positive maximum; T=c+, m=min(-w0(c-),w0(c+))>0. Set epsilon=min(1/4,3m/[4(exp(3T^2)-1)]), alpha=epsilon^(-1/2). Let w_epsilon solve w''+w'/t+w^3-epsilon*w=0 with initial(1,0), and u(r)=alpha*w_epsilon(alpha*r).
findings.assumptions: C1: smooth odd f, negative on(0,1), positive on(1,infinity). C2:F=s^4/4-s^2/2 has unique positive zero sqrt2. C3:-f'(0)=1. C7:h2=4(s^3-s), threshold1. C4 also holds:f'(1)=2. Section2 allows n=2. The constructed global solution has at least2 and finitely many simple zeros.
findings.complete_check: Energy and radial flux give finite c-,c+ and |w0|≤1. Perturbed energy gives |w_epsilon|≤1. The Volterra difference inequality yields |w_epsilon-w0|(t)≤epsilon/3*(exp(3T*t)-1)≤m/4 on[0,T], hence2zeros. The finite-zero proof uses valid cubic monotonicity above sqrt2 and the increasing weight r^(2n-3)=r; both positive-energy and zero-energy limits contradict infinitely many zeros. A critical point c between first2zeros lies before the largestzero.
findings.checked_result: At n=2, P2(r)=r^2u'(r)^2 and -(P/r^2)'=2u'^2/r. Both equal0 at c.
findings.alternative_readings: An implicit n≥3 restriction would avoid the example, but Section2 explicitly enlarges the dimension range and does not reinstate that restriction before the proposition.
findings.impact_limit: False broader preliminary assertion only. Main Theorems1–2 and Section5 impose n≥3, so this counterexample has no demonstrated core dependency at the main parameters.
findings.repair_status: Exact n=2 nonnegative identities with equality at critical points verified. Restricting strict statement to n>2 excludes this example; no complete repair of all Section2 generalizations is claimed.

acceptance_check.claim_location: Section2 domain/C1-C4 PDF6/printed250; definitions(2.18),(2.20) PDF12/256; Proposition2.5(iii)/C7 PDF13/257 and critical-point proof PDF14/258; finite-zero proof PDF9-11/253-255; identity(A.8) PDF41/285; main theorem scope PDF4-5/248-249.
acceptance_check.hypotheses: For n=2,f(s)=s^3-s,F=s^4/4-s^2/2, C1-C3 hold with b=1,alpha*=sqrt2,-f'(0)=1. C7 gives h2=4(s^3-s) with threshold1. C4 also holds since f'(1)=2. Section2 explicitly permits real n>1 and does not reinstate n>=3 before the proposition.
acceptance_check.decisive_check: For the unperturbed regular radial cubic equation, decreasing energy bounds |w0|<=1 and the flux(tw0')'=-tw0^3 proves a finite first negative minimum c- and following positive maximum c+. Set T=c+,m=min(-w0(c-),w0(c+))>0 and epsilon=min(1/4,3m/[4(exp(3T^2)-1)]). The perturbed energy keeps |w_epsilon|<=1 and the Volterra/Gronwall estimate gives D(t)<=epsilon/3*(exp(3Tt)-1)<=m/4 on[0,T]. Hence u(r)=epsilon^(-1/2)w_epsilon(epsilon^(-1/2)r) solves the actual n=2 cubic IVP and has at least two simple zeros. The independent finite-zero proof applies to this cubic n=2 case: a positive limiting energy yields divergent harmonic dissipation; a zero limiting energy makes the weighted energy r^2E eventually lose a fixed multiple of each late critical radius, using the increasing weight r^(2n-3)=r and negative F on[1/2,1]. Thus a critical point between the first two zeros lies before the largest zero. At that point P2=r^2u'^2=0 and -(P/r^2)'=2u'^2/r=0, contrary to strict positivity.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: The n=2 example is excluded from Theorems1-2 and the main n>=3 uniqueness argument. General nonlinearity monotonicity was not assumed: the finite-zero argument uses the verified cubic monotonicity above sqrt2. A decimal initial datum or numerical integration is unnecessary because epsilon and alpha are precisely defined real numbers.
acceptance_check.repair_check: For n=2 the exact nonnegative identities, with equality at critical points, hold. Restricting the strict assertion to n>2 excludes the example; this does not certify all other generalized Section2 statements.
acceptance_check.severity_reason: The false assertion lies in the explicitly enlarged preliminary dimensional range; the counterexample establishes no core damage at the main n>=3 parameters. Minor is therefore the supported grade.

acceptance_summary: Retain the Minor dimensional-scope finding. The fully specified n=2 solution satisfies the written assumptions and largest-zero qualification of Proposition2.5(iii), but lies outside the main n>=3 uniqueness theorems.
